canonicalLine: Floor plans as code. Your AI writes ArchLang; the compiler draws a precise, dimensioned plan and tells it what's wrong.
todo: The Cursor and VS Code one-click MCP install links (cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install and vscode:mcp/install) on docs-site/mcp.md and the README follow the vendors' docs and are not yet checked by hand in those apps; they stay out of the doors until they are.

chatgpt.label: ArchLang app in ChatGPT
chatgpt.example: Draw a two-bedroom flat of about 75 m² as an ArchLang plan, and check it.
chatgpt.returns: What comes back: the compiled plan, each room labelled with its area, and any problems the compiler found.

claudeai.label: claude.ai connector
claudeai.note: no install; add as a custom connector
steps: Click + Add, then Add custom connector.
Name it ArchLang, paste the server URL and click Continue.
Review the authentication settings, click Continue, choose No sign in, then click Add.
claudeai.plansNote: These are the steps on Pro and Max. On Team or Enterprise, an Owner adds it under Organization settings > Connectors (see the help page).

agent.label: Your coding agent
agent.claudeCodeHttp: claude mcp add --transport http archlang https://mcp.archlang.uk/mcp

agentPrompt: 2. Run: npx -y @chanmeng666/archlang spec   (read it before writing anything)
3. Write my floor plan as plan.arch from this brief: <describe rooms, areas, adjacencies>
then describe plan.arch --json, validate plan.arch --strict --json (same prefix); fix, recompile
5. Run: npx -y @chanmeng666/archlang finish plan.arch, then compile again to export.
Starting from a photo or PDF? Read https://archlang.uk/from-an-image. To change one room without moving the others, use `impact --lock` (https://archlang.uk/edit-one-room).
